note:
The subject is the required check of #988: a pull request from outside the project that changes a sensitive path (tools/ci/sensitive-paths.txt) is red until a trusted reviewer (owner, member, collaborator) has approved it as a review on the head commit. The approval is bound to the commit GitHub recorded it against (the review's commit_id), so a push after it, or one second before it was submitted, leaves the head unapproved. The decision lives in tools/ci/sensitive-paths.sh, run by the `Sensitive paths` job of .github/workflows/sensitive-paths.yml from the base commit.

Cycle 1 of the review replaced the first mechanism, a label: the `labeled` event carries the head at the moment the label lands, so a push just before it was approved unread. The label's mutations went with it.

Each mutation removes one refusal and names the test whose input fails that refusal only. Several refusals exit with the same code 2 (no approval, a stale approval, a reviewer blocking), so every test asserts the reason as well as the code: the mutation that ignores a blocking review on an approval-then-request sequence keeps exit 2 and loses the reason.

Cycle 2 added trust bound to who can push to the head (the head in this repository or in the author's own fork; a deleted fork is judged as outside) and made a review by a deleted account count for nothing instead of making the list unjudgeable.

After #997 (2026-11-19) the approval starts no run: its green run sat beside the push's red one and the merge stayed blocked until the red run was re-run. The workflow listens to dismissals only, and every refusal an approval answers names the run to re-run.

What this does not falsify: that GitHub runs this workflow at all, that the job name stays the required context (the ruleset names it since #994), how the review UI fills commit_id when the head moved under the reviewer (not observed on a real pull request), and anything a pull request achieves by rewriting the workflow itself, which the workflow's header says this check cannot stop.

mutations.label: every author is trusted whatever their association, so an outside pull request, Dependabot's included, passes on any path with no review as long as its head is in this repository or in its author's fork
mutations.replace: | if ($t | index($p.author_association)) == null and false then "outside"

mutations.label: a pattern holding `*` never matches: go.mod and mise.toml are still caught, but .github/, tools/ci, tools/review, tools/testplan, the scripts and the requirement files catch nothing
a renamed file is judged on its new path only, so moving a workflow out of .github/ (a deletion of that workflow) passes
the file list is judged however short it is, so a pull request past the API's 3000-file ceiling is passed on the files that happened to be listed
a head that moved during the run is judged anyway, so the check run of the event's commit carries a verdict drawn from another commit's files and reviews
an approval counts whatever commit it was given on, so commits pushed after it, or one second before it, merge unread
a reviewer from outside the project counts as trusted, so the contributor's friend approves the change
mutations.replace: | select(.author_association as $a | $trusted | index($a) != null or true)

mutations.label: a trusted reviewer's request for changes blocks nothing while another trusted reviewer approves
the earliest review of a reviewer decides instead of the latest, so an approval followed by a request for changes still approves
a dismissed review is not a decision, so an approval given before a review that was later dismissed comes back

paths are printed raw: a path holding a newline puts a line starting with `::` in the log, and only the stop-commands block would then stand between it and the runner's command parser; the test holds the stronger property that no such line is printed at all
the job is renamed, so its check run no longer carries the name the ruleset requires: a renamed job stops being required in silence
the workflow no longer wakes when an approval is dismissed, so the run the maintainer re-ran after approving stays green on the head commit after the approval is withdrawn
the author's association alone decides trust again, so a collaborator's pull request from a branch of a stranger's fork passes every push the stranger makes, unread
a payload with no author login is compared anyway, and with no head repository either both sides of `owner == author` are null: a member's pull request is trusted on nothing
mutations.replace: elif (($base | type) != "string" or ($author | type) != "string") and false then "unknown"

mutations.label: a review by a deleted account (`user: null`) counts: its request for changes, grouped under a null login, blocks an approved head
the approval starts a run of its own again: green beside the push's red run, it unblocks nothing (measured on #997) and tells the maintainer the check was re-run
the refusal no longer says that the red run has to be re-run after the approval, so the maintainer approves and waits on a merge that stays blocked
mutations.find: approve the pull request (Files changed, Review changes, Approve), $(rerun_hint).
mutations.replace: approve the pull request (Files changed, Review changes, Approve)$(rerun_hint >/dev/null).

mutations.label: GITHUB_RUN_ID is printed in the log without being checked as digits

a trigger that runs in the base repository with a write token joins the workflow (here workflow_dispatch, in the inline form a check on a trailing colon misses), which the closed list of triggers refuses
